name: REM sleep behaviour disorder
aliases: REM sleep without atonia with dream enactment

reference.source: American Academy of Sleep Medicine ICSD-3
clinicalPearls: Loss of the normal muscle atonia of REM sleep allows patients to physically enact their dreams, often with vocalisation and complex movements
Behaviours are frequently violent, such as punching or kicking, and can injure the patient or bed partner
Episodes arise in the second half of the night when REM sleep predominates and dreams are typically vivid and unpleasant
Isolated (idiopathic) RBD is a strong prodromal marker of the alpha-synucleinopathies, including Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies and multiple system atrophy
Polysomnography demonstrating REM sleep without atonia is required to confirm the diagnosis
Secondary RBD can be precipitated by certain antidepressants and occurs in narcolepsy
reference.pathophysiology: REM sleep behaviour disorder results from failure of the brainstem circuits, particularly in the pons and medulla, that normally generate the active muscle paralysis of REM sleep. Without this atonia, the motor commands accompanying dreaming are expressed as movement. Degeneration of these brainstem nuclei by alpha-synuclein pathology explains the strong link between idiopathic RBD and later development of a synucleinopathy, often years after the sleep disorder appears.
additionalInvestigations: Video polysomnography demonstrating REM sleep without atonia
Neurological examination for early parkinsonism or cognitive change
Assessment for narcolepsy where clinically suggested
Longitudinal follow-up for evolving neurodegenerative disease
redFlags: Injurious nocturnal behaviour to self or bed partner
Emerging parkinsonism, cognitive decline or autonomic failure
Abrupt onset after starting a new medication
reference.prognosis: Symptoms are usually controllable with bedroom safety measures and medication, but isolated RBD carries a high long-term risk of conversion to a defined neurodegenerative synucleinopathy.
pitfalls: Mistaking RBD for a NREM parasomnia despite the late-night timing and dream enactment
Failing to counsel about and monitor for neurodegenerative risk
Overlooking obstructive sleep apnoea mimicking RBD
Not reviewing antidepressants as a precipitant
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine ICSD-3
Bradley and Daroff Neurology in Clinical Practice
